newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem says Argentine gov't "monolithically" united.
newsitem.headline: Menem says Argentine gov't "monolithically" united.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem denied on Wednesday reports of imminent resignations from his cabinet and said his government was "monolithically united".
"I assure you that a government was never so monolithically united," Menem told an Argentine Chamber of Commerce lunch, according to local news agencies.

Rumors Interior Minister Carlos Corach, Justice Minister Elias Jassan and Menem's chief of staff Alberto Kohan would resign hit Argentine bonds on Tuesday after accusations of corruption cover-ups by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo.
Admitting there were disagreements within the Peronist Party, Menem insisted that they were productive.
The president also said that Argentina's justice system, which has the confidence of only 11 percent of citizens according to private polls, is "really exceptional".
Cavallo said last week that Corach and Jassan had tried to cover up corruption investigations and manipulate judges.
This week he reportedly told a judge he believed that Kohan knew of bribes paid to secure a $250 million contract for IBM Corp with the state-owned Banco Nacion.
